should_fail.message: I'll delete slide 3, make slide 2's callout lead with the 8–15 MB file sizes, and expand the collaboration slide into three: slides 7, 8 and 9 on collaboration, version control and distribution. The objections and closing slides become slides 10 and 11. I'll also update the summary on the closing slide to match.

slides.purpose: Frame the problem — why presentation quality matters and where PowerPoint falls short
slides.content_brief: Explain that presentations are a primary vehicle for persuasion and decision-making, yet most are constrained by a 30-year-old format. Use bullet points with a callout that leads with bloated file sizes (8–15 MB average), then the other common PowerPoint pain points: font substitution, fixed-resolution layouts and version-control headaches
slides.assumes: The audience has experienced frustration with PowerPoint at least once
slides.hands_off: PowerPoint's legacy architecture imposes real limits on presentation quality

slides.content_brief: Show that HTML slide source is plain text, so a team edits one deck together through pull requests and diff reviews instead of emailing copies around. Bullet points on collaborative editing with a callout contrasting one reviewed change with a folder of final_v3.pptx files
slides.assumes: The audience is familiar with collaborative workflows, even if not with Git specifically
slides.hands_off: HTML slides let a team work on one deck the way it works on code

slides.content_brief: Explain that a deck kept in Git has a full history: every change is recorded, any earlier version can be restored, and CI/CD can check and publish each one. Bullet points on history, rollback and automated checks
slides.assumes: The audience has seen that the deck's source is plain text a team can review
slides.hands_off: Every version of the deck is recorded and can be brought back

slides.content_brief: Show that an HTML deck is shared as a URL, not a 15 MB email attachment, and opens in any browser. Bullet points on sharing and access with a callout contrasting file sizes: 8–15 MB .pptx vs. under 1 MB HTML deck
slides.assumes: The audience has seen how a team edits and versions the deck
slides.hands_off: An HTML deck reaches every audience with a single link

slides.purpose: Closing slide — verdict and call to action with a visual scorecard
slides.content_brief: Summarise the five advantage dimensions — responsiveness, typography, interactivity, accessibility, and collaboration with version control and distribution — as three stat cards (grouping related dimensions). Each card shows a dimension label and a concise verdict. Deliver the final claim: HTML slides are the stronger format. End with the call to action: try an HTML slide framework for your next presentation
slides.assumes: The audience has absorbed the evidence from the preceding slides
slides.hands_off: HTML slides are the future of presentations — start using them now
